title: slot-claim signature covers only ordinal/IID/superframe_id; slots array forgeable; no claim_seq replay gate or expiry
description: coap_slot_coord.c:316-337 reconstructs the signed message as SLOT_CLAIM:%02X:%IID:%08X from ordinal, gateway_iid, superframe_id only — NOT the slots array. GCP-6.5 (spec/08:117-160) mandates COSE_Sign1 over the full claim payload including slots/expiry/claim_seq. An adversary who captures one legitimate claim can re-attach the identical signature to a different slots array (same ordinal/IID/superframe_id): schnorr48_verify passes and process_claim registers attacker-chosen slots under the victim IID, with lowest-IID conflict resolution favoring the forgery (airtime hijack / scheduling DoS attributed to a legit gateway). Also missing per spec GCP-6.5 step 7 (expiry > now check; struct lichen_slot_claim has no expiry field) and step 8 + claim_seq persistence table (MUST reject claim_seq <= cached; no claim_seq field or replay cache). Fix: sign the canonical CBOR encoding of the whole claim (or implement the COSE_Sign1 envelope), add expiry + NV-persisted claim_seq; align response codes while touching (spec step 10 says 2.04 Changed, impl returns 2.01; step 11 says 4.09 with winning gateway's claim, impl sends NULL payload). Design with the sibling bead (decoder cannot carry signatures).
close_reason: ALL children closed: the five fix children (slots-array forgery, expiry, claim_seq, response codes, vectors) landed across this session and prior worker rounds; child .6 (cross-validation review) verified three-way parity this round — Python 6 passed/3 documented-skips + 23 format tests, Rust 2/2 corpus + 252 lib + 21 tdma_beacon, C coap_slot_claim 1/1. The parent's security claims (signature covers full payload incl. slots; expiry; claim_seq replay gate; 2.04/4.03/4.09 response codes) are implemented and tested in all three implementations. Residuals tracked: yiv0 (4.09 response code), c366 (orphaned C path), 104v (Python kid-binding divergence), qe1t/ljgs (wire sizing for signed DIOs), l1qw.22 (closed this session).
